sources: Australian Museum, Platypus: found in eastern Australia; one of only five living egg-laying mammals (monotremes); males have a venomous spur on each hind ankle, the venom causes severe pain but is not known to kill people; the bill is packed with electroreceptors and touch receptors, and it hunts underwater with eyes, ears and nostrils closed; adults have no teeth and grind food with horny pads; mothers have no nipples, milk seeps from patches on the belly; https://australian.museum/learn/animals/mammals/platypus/
Anich et al. 2020, Mammalia, Biofluorescence in the platypus: platypus fur glows blue-green under ultraviolet light; https://doi.org/10.1515/mammalia-2020-0027
Ordoñez et al. 2008, Genome Research / University of Sydney: the platypus lacks a true stomach; the gullet connects straight to the intestine; https://doi.org/10.1101/gr.7096208

Natural History Museum (London), The platypus specimen: when the first platypus specimen reached Britain (described by George Shaw, 1799), naturalists suspected it might be a fake stitched together from different animals; https://www.nhm.ac.uk/discover/platypus.html

beats.say: No stomach. Lays eggs. And it glows under a blacklight.
The platypus. A duck bill, on a furry mammal.
It lives in rivers and streams in eastern Australia.
Look inside. Its food tube goes straight to its gut.
Shine an ultraviolet light on it, and its fur glows blue-green.
And the males have venom spurs on their back legs.
A mammal that lays eggs, glows, and stings.
